title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Workshop on Measuring International Development, Advancing Equity
location: GISB - Room Number: 1060
description: Humanity stands at a crossroads. While we have made incredible strides in human development, we also face existential threats—from climate change and pandemics to growing polarization and inequality. To overcome these threats, we must work together to advance a coherent vision of human development centered on guaranteeing every person a dignified, or at least minimally good, life. This workshop addresses the conceptual and practical gaps in how we measure social progress. A narrow focus on GDP is no longer sufficient; it is distribution-insensitive and fails to capture the non-market values essential for mutual flourishing. This workshop will explore how to think about development, develop better metrics, and put them into practice.

title: Death Cafe
description:
A Death Cafe is a group-directed discussion of death with no agenda, ideology, objectives, or themes. It is a discussion group rather than grief support or counseling session. Death Cafes have spread quickly around the world. Over 16,500 Death Cafes are held in 85 countries. All are volunteer-run.
The monthly Death Cafe at Morgenstern Books is run by co-hosts Rick Clayton and Casey Stover. Rick Clayton is a hospice chaplain, end-of life doula, and musician who enjoys playing harp, cello, and guitar for his clients. Casey Stover is a Certified Family Life Educator whose professional work often exists adjacent to death and grief, shaping her belief in the importance of accessible spaces to normalize honest conversation and community care.
You can find our Death Cafe at the back corner of the bookstore, near the restrooms, on the last Tuesday of every month at 7 pm.

Confidentiality: Safety is built when we can trust that what we share will remain with the people with whom we choose to share.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

The campaign began after a ruling by the Italian Supreme Court to overturn a rape conviction because the justices felt that since the victim was wearing tight jeans she must have helped the person who raped her remove them, thereby implying consent. title: "Art as Inquiry," A Gallery Show
location: Pillar Arts Alliance Center
description:
Artists for Climate Awareness invites people of all ages to experience “Art as Inquiry,” a juried climate‑art exhibition on view April 2–29 at the Pillar Arts Alliance Center in Bloomington, IN and online. Featuring 2‑D and 3‑D works from artists across several states, this Earth Month exhibition explores urgent climate and environmental issues through creative expression and community engagement.

Art, especially, can turn scientific knowledge into experiences that resonate emotionally—offering insights that facts and figures alone can’t always reach. When these perspectives come together, they open up fresh ways of seeing and help people connect more deeply with complex ideas. “Art as Inquiry” invites visitors to encounter climate research, ecological change, and environmental justice through the lens of artistic imagination.

Beginning April 19, artwork from the Climate Co‑lab \(Brushes for a Better Planet\) joins the exhibition, displayed alongside the Art as Inquiry works.

Earth Month Events \(Free; Public Invited\):

April 12, 2–3 pm – Nature Walk, a musical and narrative performance led by IU Jacobs School of Music student Thejas Mirle and four composers, with narration by Distinguished IU Biology Professor Roger Hangarter.

April 12, 3–5 pm – Reception for the member climate‑art exhibition; prizes awarded. 🌱

April 19, 3–6 pm – Climate Co‑lab Reception \+ Nature Walk performance; brief introductions of artists and partners.

Gallery Hours: • Thu–Sat: 2–8 pm • Sun: 12–6 pm Pillar Arts Alliance Center, College Mall, Bloomington. Free admission.

description: Repertoire  Julia Wolfe: Tell me everything (1994)Yuting Tan: Amnesia (2023)Emma Cardon-Wake: GIRLHOOD (2025, premiere)*  *Georgina Joshi Composition CommissionAbout the ConductorDavid Dzubay's compositions have been performed in the United States, Europe, Canada, Mexico, and Asia by the symphony orchestras of Aspen, Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Cincinnati, Detroit, Fort Wayne, Guangxi, Guiyang, Honolulu, Kansas City, Louisville, Memphis, Minnesota, Oregon, Oakland, St. Louis and Vancouver; the American Composers Orchestra, National Symphonies of Ireland and Mexico, New World Symphony, National Repertory Orchestra, and New York Youth Symphony; and ensembles including the Grossman Ensemble, Le Nouvel Ensemble Moderne, Onix, Manhattan and St. Louis Brass Quintets, Voices of Change, the Alexander, Orion and Pacifica string quartets, the League/ISCM, Earplay, and the San Francisco Contemporary Music Players. His music has been championed by conductors including James DePreist, George Hanson, Keith Lockhart, David Loebel, Michael Morgan, Eiji Oue, Richard Pittman, Iván del Prado, Mark Russell Smith, Lawrence Leighton Smith, Michael Stern, Carl Topilow, David Wiley, Kirk Trevor, Thomas Wilkins, and David Zinman. Honors include two Fromm Music Foundation commissions; Guggenheim, MacDowell, Yaddo, Copland House, and Djerassi fellowships; the Kuhmo Chamber Music Festival Composition Competition, Indianapolis Chamber Orchestra Composition Competition, Utah Arts Festival Commission, William Revelli and Walter Beeler Memorial Prizes, Wayne Peterson Prize; and grants from the Aaron Copland Fund for Music for two portrait CDs. Currently professor of music and director of the New Music Ensemble at the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music in Bloomington, Dzubay was previously on the faculty of the University of North Texas in Denton. Since 2011, he has taught composition for three weeks each summer at the Brevard Music Center. From 1995 to 1998, he served as composer-consultant to the Minnesota Orchestra and during the 2005-06 season, he was Meet the Composer/American Symphony Orchestra League Music Alive Composer-in-Residence with the Green Bay Symphony Orchestra. Dzubay has conducted at the Tanglewood, Aspen, and June in Buffalo festivals as well as the National Symphony of Columbia, Grossman Ensemble, League of Composers Orchestra, Pittsburgh New Music Ensemble, Music from China, and Voices of Change.The Georgina Joshi Composition Commission Award  A vision of Louise Addicott-Joshi and made possible by a gift from The Georgina Joshi Foundation, the annual Georgina Joshi Composition Commission is awarded to a student composer in support of a new work for solo voice and instrumental ensemble to be premiered and recorded by the New Music Ensemble. The award is presented in conjunction with the Composition Department's annual Dean's Prizes.Georgina Joshi earned her bachelor's degree in music (with honors) from the Royal College of Music in London and pursued a master's degree in the Jacobs School of Music. While at IU, Joshi appeared as a soloist in major choral performances and IU Opera Theater productions. An enthusiastic performer, she was featured in a variety of regional ensembles and festivals, and appeared as a soloist in England, Wales, Romania, and Greece.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Emily Zazulia: "Music for the eyes? Rethinking 'Augenmusik'"
location: MAXWELL HALL - Room Number: Grand Hall
description: Abstract: Late fifteenth-century music occasionally asks performers to read its notation in unusual ways— from slowing down a melodic line to turning it backwards or upside-down, or even omitting certain notes or rests. These visual elements are integral dimensions of the work's conceptual whole. Yet they have never sat easily with music scholars and critics for whom music is, by definition, that which reaches the ears. In 1912, Alfred Einstein gave this discomfort a name:Augenmusik, music for the eyes.Einstein's coinage, it turns out, says more about 1912 than about 1480. This paper traces the historiography of that term, arguing that each successive framework—from Einstein's formalist dismissal to the modernist reclamation of the score as visual object—has projected its own assumptions about the relationship between the senses onto a repertoire that operated by a different logic entirely. That logic, I argue, was intellectual rather than sensory: for fifteenth-century musicians, engaging with notation was not a deviation from aesthetic experience but a form of it, a prized dimension of what it meant to encounter a piece of music.Augenmusikearns its place, finally, as an admission: that notation, here, was doing something the modern discipline had no other language for.Emily Zazulia (https://music.berkeley.edu/people/emily-zazulia)is Associate Professor of Music at the University of California, Berkeley. Her first monographWhere Sight Meets Sound: The Poetics of Late-Medieval Music Writing(Oxford, 2021) received the Early Music Award from the American Musicological Society and the Emerging Scholar Book Award from the Society for Music Theory. She has received other awards and fellowships from the National Endowment for the Humanities, the American Council of Learned Societies, the American Musicological Society, the Medieval Academy of America, the Renaissance Society of America, Harvard University's Villa I Tatti, and the Hellman Foundation. Current major projects include a monograph on popular song and ideas of the secular, a co-edited volume on the composer Josquin des Prez, and a digital project on Mapping the Musical Renaissance.Emily Zazulia's visit to Indiana University is made possible through generous support from the College of Arts and Sciences, the Department of Musicology, and the Department of Music Theory.

title: U.S. Economic Cooperation with Nations in the Middle East and Central Asia: Working Towards Regional Stabilities
location: GISB - Room Number: 3067
description: Nations of the Middle East and Central Asia have emerged over the last decade as important partners to the United States both economically and strategically. Economic ties have expanded with the United States through two-way direct investments, third country cooperation, collaboration in innovation technologies and supply chain diversifications. At the same time, the economic integration of these two regions has also increased, with both state and private investment from the GCC countries into Turkey and Central Asia. In the geopolitical sphere, Middle Eastern nations seek to maintain good relationships with China and Russia, while enhancing ties with Washington. Central Asian countries seek to expand political and economic links with the United States to diversify from Russia and China. This discussion will focus on the business and economic ties between America and these regions as they look toward regional stability and global economic competitiveness.     Khush Choksy is senior vice president of International Member Relations at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. In this capacity, he oversees member engagement and fundraising across the International Division and its over 30 business councils and programs. He also leads the Chamber's programs in the Middle East, Türkiye, and Central Asia.  As the head of International Member Relations, Choksy is responsible for member services across all the U.S. Chamber's companies that are part of its International Division.  As senior vice president of the Middle East and Türkiye Department, Choksy's responsibilities include oversight of several bilateral business councils and programs. Under his leadership, the Middle East portfolio has expanded to become the U.S. Chamber's largest international program and represents over 250 companies. Choksy also led the effort to integrate the U.S.-India Business Council into the U.S. Chamber.  Before joining the Chamber, Choksy was a director at Chemonics International. There, he led teams developing economic ties between the United States and the Middle East. He lived and worked in Jordan for seven years, and also lived and worked in India, Sri Lanka, and the U.K. Prior to that, Choksy worked for the Parsons Corporation. He is a recognized thought leader on the role of international business in the global economy.  Choksy received his M.B.A. in strategic management from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania and his B.A., magna cum laude, from Hamilton College. He lives with his wife and daughter in Chevy Chase, Maryland.

location: Scott & Connie Ferguson Crestmont Boys & Girls Club: 1111 w 12th St.
description:
Live auction, dinner, and empowering conversation with emcee Dana Starr Cummings & keynote speaker Jodi Bondi Norgaard.
An immensely beneficial and world-class program that directly impacts Club females, SMART Girls is a health, fitness, prevention/education and self-enhancement program for young women ages 8-17.
SMART Girls helps young women reach their full potential. Through dynamic sessions, group activities, field trips and mentoring opportunities with adult women, Club girls enjoy life-changing opportunities to build skills for eating right, staying physically fit, getting good health care, and developing positive relationships.
Other topics addressed through the SMART Girls programming with older girls include how the media influences attitudes about females, date rape and sexual harassment, sexually transmitted diseases, sexual myths and truths, getting regular gynecological care and the physical and emotional changes girls experience in their lifetime.
SMART Girls, STRONG Women is an annual event where funds to support SMART Girls programming are raised through various avenues including ticket sales, sponsorships, a live auction component and a concluding fund-a-need. This specific event, typically held during the springtime, has been a staple for the Club since 2016, and is traditionally a sold-out spectacle with nearly 300 people in attendance.
During the business-casual event, it will focuses on the importance of positive female-imagery to young girls in today’s world. The event also includes a buffet-style dinner with dessert.

title: Femina Natura
location: Pillar Arts Alliance Center,2894 East 3rd Street, Bloomington, IN 47401, USA
description:
Grace/Butedma Gonso is a Buryat-Mongol artist living in rural Indiana. She prefers working

in oils with rich colors. Her depictions of her cultural heritage and scenes of rural living are

vibrant and expressive. Nature is her greatest inspiration. She enjoys capturing seasonal

changes in nature and local farm and garden images.

‘’I mainly paint nature scenes, avoiding the details as details can be tedious. So most of my

paintings are wide, expansive, open views of landscape with certain moods and atmospheres

that I try to depict. I enjoy putting down rhythmic, repeated brush strokes that come out

freely through my intuition.

HOWEVER, every once in a while I paint something different. An event, a dream, a movie, a

book or a quote would seed an idea that results in an abstract, narrative painting. They tend to

appear somewhat somber, perhaps expressions of a mother’s fear and worry and a helpless

feeling towards the future of all living things. We know that we caused much destruction to

the planet, Mother Earth, our only vessel on which we all travel through the void.

This is a show of these paintings.’’

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

Five original collages by graphic designer Pouya Jahanshahi are at the center of the exhibition. Jahanshahi collaborated with Project Archivist Jason Byrne, who shaped the exhibition's themes and selected archival content. title: Strategic Thinking in U.S.-Africa Policy and Intelligence (w/ LUNCH)
location: GLOBAL & INTERNATIONAL STUDIES BUILDING - Room Number: 1118
description: Event Description:  How do policymakers and intelligence officers navigate complex decisions in Africa and beyond?  Join Judd Devermont (https://www.csis.org/people/judd-devermont), former National Intelligence Officer for Africa and former Senior Director for African Affairs at the White House, for a live, scenario-driven session on strategy, risk, and global policymaking.  Devermont spent over a decade in the intelligence community, advised two administrations, authored the U.S. Strategy toward Sub-Saharan Africa, and directed major initiatives shaping billions in infrastructure, digital connectivity, and energy investments.This is not a lecture. You will work through a real-world scenario: African states balancing relationships with the U.S. and China while managing domestic political and development pressures.  You'll assess risk, identify second- and third-order effects, evaluate trade-offs, and recommend a course of action.What you'll gain:      Insight into how intelligence and policy intersect          Frameworks to anticipate unintended consequences          How analysis translates into real-world decisions          A window into careers in intelligence, government, and think tanks    Lunch will be provided! Come ready to debate, analyze, and defend your conclusions in an interactive, off-the-record setting.

title: Tour of Thomas Hart Benton's Indiana Murals
location: AUDITORIUM - Room Number: Hall of Murals
description: This tour visitsThe Hall of Murals at IU Auditorium  IU Cinema  Woodburn Hall  About the Indiana Murals:  Thomas Hart Benton was commissioned to paint murals depicting Indiana history for the Indiana state pavilion at the 1933 World's Fair in Chicago. The dramatic 250-foot long mural, which originally wrapped around the entire exhibition hall at the World's Fair, depicts the social, economic, and cultural history of Indiana from mound building to the 1930s. After several years of storage following the fair, the panels were given to Indiana University in 1938, where they were installed in three locations on the Bloomington campus. About Your Guide:  Jim Davis is a Senior Lecturer in the Kelley School of Business, in the department of Management and Entrepreneurship. He has been serving as a docent and museum guide at the IU Eskenazi Museum of Art for the past ten years.     Know Before You GoThis tour visits three locations on campus. Please let us know if an elevator and wheelchair accessible route will be needed.   Plan to arrive at least 5 minutes beforehand to check in.For a discounted parking rate for the Indiana Memorial Union parking lot, visit the Eskenazi Museum of Art before or after this tour and ask Guest Services, at the Information Desk on the first floor, to stamp your parking voucher.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Lincoln's Declaration: How He Interpreted--and Defended--Our Founding Document
location: Unitarian Universalist Church, 2120 N Fee Ln, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description: In honor of its 250th Anniversary, John Schilb, Culbertson Chair and Professor Emeritus of English, will analyze Abraham Lincoln’s rhetoric regarding the Declaration of Independence. Many of Lincoln's opponents (e.g., Stephen Douglas and Jefferson Davis) either ridiculed the Declaration's claim that "all men are created equal" or believed that it applied just to whites. Lincoln maintained that "all" really did mean everyone. Only gradually, however, was he willing to consider Black people his social peers. Statements that he made during his debates with Douglas reflect this complex attitude. And even the Gettysburg Address does not assume that the Declaration's message has a future. Indeed, that speech called the Declaration's claim about equality a "proposition" to be tested. That is, Lincoln saw American democracy as something that might not endure. Its fate still seems in question, so his take on the Declaration remains timely.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Southern Indiana Wind Ensemble Spring Concert
location: Bloomington High School North Auditorium, 3901 N Kinser Pike, Bloomington
description:
Conductor: Stephen W. Pratt
This concert features music that celebrates American music in many ways.
The Symphonic Concert March is by an Italian composer, but was rescued from obscurity by Nicholas Falcone, one of two Italian brothers who came to America as teenagers and made a huge impact on the American concert band world in many ways. The Alfred Reed Ballade features our guest soloist, Dr. Thomas Walsh, from the Jacobs School of Music faculty, an outstanding saxophonist. Florence Price’s Adoration, a transcription of her organ piece, is a beautiful addition to our repertoire. David Dzubay, from the Jacobs School of Music faculty is represented with his Gloriana, Frangipana, a piece he composed. Three iconic American composers are also represented – Bernstein, Copland, and Gershwin. My hope is that every member of the audience will find at least several pieces that they want to hear and will enjoy.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Your Name Means Dream by Jose Rivera
location: Waldron Rose Firebay,122 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
AI is hauntingly current and a topic that urges us to examine its impact.
Will AI robots soon replace human caregivers for the elderly? With emotionally-charged narrative and poetic dialogue, José Rivera examines how we live and form our sense of self in a world that’s increasingly saturated with technology. It challenges all people, all identities and all faiths. How do we apply morals, values and ethics when we introduce machine over human?

Theatre legend Diane Kondrat, who moved west after performing theatre for 27 years in Bloomington, is returning to star in this production. The role of AI caregiver Stacy will be played by Valerie C. Kilmer who is making her debut with JTB.

With an extraordinary team of artists and a fascinating topic, this production promises to be a sell-out!

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Your Name Means Dream by Jose Rivera
location: Waldron Rose Firebay,122 South Walnut Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
AI is hauntingly current and a topic that urges us to examine its impact.
Will AI robots soon replace human caregivers for the elderly? With emotionally-charged narrative and poetic dialogue, José Rivera examines how we live and form our sense of self in a world that’s increasingly saturated with technology. It challenges all people, all identities and all faiths. How do we apply morals, values and ethics when we introduce machine over human?

Theatre legend Diane Kondrat, who moved west after performing theatre for 27 years in Bloomington, is returning to star in this production. The role of AI caregiver Stacy will be played by Valerie C. Kilmer who is making her debut with JTB.

With an extraordinary team of artists and a fascinating topic, this production promises to be a sell-out!

title: Hike the Trust: Canyon Forest Nature Preserve
location: Canyon Forest Nature Preserve
description: Join us for a guided hike as part of our Hike the Trust series at Canyon Forest Nature Preserve, a rugged and scenic 68-acre preserve. Its deep ravines and sandstone outcrops are part of Greene County’s ancient bedrock, where resistant sandstones and underlying shale have been sculpted over millions of years to form dramatic canyons and slopes that support diverse plant communities, from orchids and ferns to woodland trees. Along the way, we’ll tie together how the geology influences soil, water flow, and plant distribution, helping you see the connection between rocks, soils, forests, and ecological diversity in one of Indiana’s most interesting natural areas.

title: Family Art Lab
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Studio
description: Please note that this month's Family Art Lab does not follow the second Sunday schedule.  Designed for K-12 students and their families, this event offers a fun and flexible way to spark creativity and connect with each other. All ages and experience levels are welcome!  Come and go at your own pace. We recommend planning for at least an hour to explore the gallery and make art.  Start in the Art Studio inside the Kimberly and John Simpson Center for Education on the museum's 2nd floor to pick up your Gallery Challenge. Then head to the galleries to find the artwork we'll use as inspiration for our project! When you're ready, head back to the studio for our hands-on art-making activity that everyone will love.  This program takes place every Second Sunday of the month, excluding holidays and museum closures. Each month features new artworks and materials, so there's always something fresh to explore and create!  All children must be chaperoned.Know Before You Go:Read about where to find us, where to park, accessibility, and museum guidelines.Strollers are welcome in the galleries. When carrying small children, please keep them in front of you.  To save time at the lockers, avoid bringing backpacks or large bags.  When You Arrive:If you parked in the IMU parking lot, Guest Services can validate your parking voucher for a discount.  Store any large bags in the lockers behind the Guest Services desk.  Head upstairs to the 2nd Floor and into the Simpson Center for Education to start.  When in the galleries, do not touch the artwork. Be mindful to keep body parts and anything you're carrying at least 18" away from the art.  Photography is welcome! Just no flash or selfie sticks.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Homeschool Day: America 250
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
description: Travel back in time with us to America in 1776 to meet George Washington and see the Declaration of Independence up close. Together, we'll explore the art and stories that shaped our nation's founding. Afterwards, we'll create our own colonial-inspired artwork in the studio, reflecting on the theme of "What America Means to Me."Know Before You Go:  Meet us on the 1st floor of the museum at 10 a.m. Together, we'll drop off personal items in the Simpson Center for Education before exploring the galleries. After seeing artworks that will inspire our project, we'll head back to the Roehm Family Art-Making Studio to create our own masterpieces! Don't forget to dress for a mess!  Strollers are welcome. Chaperones required. We ask that chaperones be 18 or older, with one adult for every 6 children.Parking Information:  The museum is in the pedestrian district of campus with several parking options nearby. The Indiana Memorial Union lot (900 E. 7th Street) is just a 5-minute walk diagonal to the museum, and visitors can receive 40% off parking validation at the museum's guest services desk. The East Garage (105 N. Eagleson Ave.) and Fee Lane Garage (709 N. Fee Lane) are also convenient, about an 8–10 minute walk. Learn more about parking on the Bloomington campus here (https://parking.indiana.edu/facilities/index.html).

Early season rides are shorter, and rides get longer as the season progresses. Peak season rides average 25–35 miles, depending on available daylight. Rides depart promptly at 5:45. Front and rear lights are encouraged.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

description:
“A Rock ‘n’ Roll Tribute – From Elvis to the Beatles featuring The Neverly Brothers”
The Neverly Brothers concerts take you on a guided musical VIRTUAL TOUR of the birth, near death and resurrection of rock n’ roll – from 1955 to 1965. You’ll learn rock history and be thoroughly entertained with their chronological song sequence, stories behind the music and vintage wardrobe changes. Their energetic stage show consists of show-stopping renditions of early hits by Jerry Lee Lewis, Chuck Berry, Buddy Holly, The Beatles, Rolling Stones, and more!
The first half of their concert pays tribute to the music created by the 1950s American Rock n’ Roll pioneers – which by 1960 had become a distant memory but became the inspiration for the next wave of young rock bands from Britain. The second half then pays tribute to the 1964 British Invasion bands that re-recorded the forgotten 1950s American rock music – along with lesser known early 1960s rhythm & blues songs, recorded their own original songs and pulled Rock n’ Roll from the edge of extinction by re-inventing and re-energizing it for a new generation.
Their repertoire includes spirited performances of classics like Great balls of fire, Johnny B. Goode, Wake up little Susie, Summertime blues, That’ll be the day, Twist & shout, Roll over Beethoven, Satisfaction, You really got me, Love potion #9 and many more!
It‘s not “moldy oldies”- it’s “old-school cool!” So hop aboard our virtual tour bus and fasten your seatbelts for an exciting MAGICAL HISTORY TOUR!

description: Full Moons occur when the Moon is fully illuminated by the Sun, allowing viewers on Earth to see the full circle. It's typically the brightest night of the month. The New Moon is the darkest night of the month, when dark side of the Moon faces Earth. We're going on a hike on the darkest night of the month! We will meet at the Park Office/Fire Tower Parking lot at 9pm to hike Trail 10. Please note Trail 10 should be considered very rugged in the dark and involves hiking from one of the highest elevations in the park to one of the lowest. The route is 2.2 miles and will take about two hours. Red flashlights help us preserve night vision. We have some to lend out, but it is wise to bring your own if you have one. Brown County State Park Naturalists' hike cancellation policy: Hikes will be cancelled for safety reasons. Rain by itself is not enough to cancel a hike. title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.
