title: Toddler Sports Classes
description: Playpen Sports Academy is a wonderful way to introduce your child to the world of sport and physical activity in a non-intimidating environment with a small group of other toddlers and parents. The Playpen Sports Academy Curriculum is focused on a number of different goals including teaching children how to move and use their bodies, sharing with other children, interact in social settings, follow directions, and most importantly how to have fun in a physically active environment. title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Hedwig and the Angry Inch | Granfalloon
location: IU CINEMA
description: With this boundary-breaking, trailblazing musical extravaganza, writer-director-star John Cameron Mitchell and composer-lyricist Stephen Trask bring their critically acclaimed off-Broadway rock theater hit to the screen for a film as unclassifiable as its protagonists. Raised a boy in East Berlin, Hedwig (Mitchell) undergoes a traumatic personal transformation in order to emigrate to the U.S., where she reinvents herself as an "internationally ignored" but divinely talented rock diva, characterized by Mitchell as inhabiting a "beautiful gender of one." Hedwig's story is told through an eclectic assortment of original punk anthems and power ballads by Trask, and paired with a freewheeling cinematic mosaic of music-video fantasies, animated interludes, and moments of bracing emotional realism. [95 min; musical, drama, comedy; English and German with English subtitles]

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. Or a whole day. This self-guided offering is designed to allow you to create your own educational experience. Visit all locations in one trip or come back to campus multiple times. Each Fine Arts Plaza destination has different operating hours; please consult them carefully when planning your trip. All locations are open Tuesday–Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.  Check our online event calendar at go.iu.edu/america-250 (https://go.iu.edu/america-250) for special events and additional campus celebrations of America's 250th.  To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: OWLS -
location: Sherwood Oaks Christian Church, 2700 E Rogers Rd, Bloomington, IN 47401, USA
description:

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. Or a whole day. This self-guided offering is designed to allow you to create your own educational experience. Visit all locations in one trip or come back to campus multiple times. Each Fine Arts Plaza destination has different operating hours; please consult them carefully when planning your trip. All locations are open Tuesday–Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.  Check our online event calendar at go.iu.edu/america-250 (https://go.iu.edu/america-250) for special events and additional campus celebrations of America's 250th.  To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. title: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market
location: City of Bloomington, 401 N Morton St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
The Bloomington Community Farmers' Market takes place rain or shine every Saturday, April through October, at Showers Common next to City Hall, 401 N. Morton St. in Bloomington.
April-September: 8 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
October: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
November: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m. at the Pavilion at Switchyard Park
The Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.
Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. Food and beverage artisans provide a tasteful variety of drinks, pastries, and savory dishes. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.
source: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market, Parks And Rec, WFHB Community Calendar

title: Vicki Peterson and John Cowsill
location: Brown County Playhouse, 70 S. Van Buren St, Nashville, IN, 47448, United States
description:
Vicki Peterson, a founding member of The Bangles, whose work includes the #1 hit “Walk Like An Egyptian” and several other Top 10 songs, such as “Eternal Flame”, teams up with John Cowsill, drummer/vocalist for The Beach Boys for over 23 years and original member of the platinum-selling family band, The Cowsills, to lovingly present their debut Americana album comprised of songs written by John’s late brothers, Barry and Bill Cowsill titled, Long After The Fire.
It all began with the songs…exquisitely written by John’s brothers at various points in their all-too-short lives. These ‘Roy Orbison’ meets ‘The Everly Brothers’ tunes are true gems unearthed like treasures from The Cowsill family archives.
Get ready to hear the latest tracks from their new album alongside iconic classics from The Bangles and The Cowsills all while they reveal the fascinating stories behind the music—perfect for the ultimate fans! It will be an incredible night filled with music, love, and unforgettable moments.

With special guest SAMI RIGGS. Winner of the 2025 Brown County Songwriter Showdown.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market
location: City of Bloomington, 401 N Morton St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
The Bloomington Community Farmers' Market takes place rain or shine every Saturday, April through October, at Showers Common next to City Hall, 401 N. Morton St. in Bloomington.
April-September: 8 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
October: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
November: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m. at the Pavilion at Switchyard Park
The Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.
Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. Food and beverage artisans provide a tasteful variety of drinks, pastries, and savory dishes. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.
source: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market, Parks And Rec, WFHB Community Calendar

title: Beginner/Intermediate Drawing Workshop
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Check in with Guest Services on the first floor
description: Reserve your spot. If this page says, "Registration has closed" that means the waitlist is full.SuppliesBring your favorite drawing pencil (e.g. 4B), a sketchbook or drawing paper, and a phone or device to photograph artwork (without flash) as we sketch.  Know Before You GoArrive early to find parking, check in, and get your drawing supplies ready.  At 1:55 p.m. any unclaimed reservations will be released to guests who are standing by waiting for a spot.  Where to find us, where to park, accessibility, and museum guidelines (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/your-visit.html).  This workshop is recommended for ages 12 and up. Anyone under 18, who is not an IU student, must be accompanied by an adult.  When You ArriveCheck in with Guest Services at the information desk on the first floor, even if you come often and even if you are late. We appreciate having an accurate attendance count.  Store all backpacks and large bags before entering the galleries. A small handbag may be carried at your side.  Get your supplies ready. Attach an 18x24" piece of newsprint to a drawing board.  Cancellations  This workshop often has a waitlist. Please use the cancellation link included with your confirmation email if your plans change.About the Instructor  John Cheek has taught credit and non-credit classes for eight years in portrait painting, landscape painting, palette knife painting, life drawing, beginning drawing, and advanced drawing, as well as in design. He volunteers his time and expertise to facilitate drawing workshops at the Eskenazi Museum of Art.
source: Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Arts & Humanities Institute

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. Or a whole day. This self-guided offering is designed to allow you to create your own educational experience. Visit all locations in one trip or come back to campus multiple times. Each Fine Arts Plaza destination has different operating hours; please consult them carefully when planning your trip. All locations are open Tuesday–Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.  Check our online event calendar at go.iu.edu/america-250 (https://go.iu.edu/america-250) for special events and additional campus celebrations of America's 250th.  To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: I Ride
location: Sherwood Oaks Christian Church, 2700 E Rogers Rd, Bloomington, IN 47401, USA
description:
The iRide is a no drop ride with regroup points geared toward the rider wanting to push the pace a bit without being race oriented. 16-18mph avg on most rides. We typically follow the OWLS group route and add some extra miles/climbs in the second half of the route allowing folks to start out with us and if we are too fast they can drop back to the OWLS group. All interested in a brisker pace are welcome!

Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership of up to one month and sign a liability waiver before participating in a club ride. https://secure.getmeregistered.com/get_information.php?event_id=141883

title: OWLS -
location: Sherwood Oaks Christian Church, 2700 E Rogers Rd, Bloomington, IN 47401, USA
description:
Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership, good for up to one month, and which includes electronically signing a liability waiver, prior to participation.

The “Older, Wiser, and a Little Slower” group emphasizes moderate rides and a route planned in advance that is posted on the ride calendar. This is a no drop ride for a range of intermediate riders—it is not a beginner’s ride. Average pace is 12-15 mph which includes hills. Regroup points are discussed in advance. Early season rides are shorter, and rides get longer as the season progresses. Peak season rides average 25–35 miles, depending on available daylight. Rides depart promptly at 5:45. Front and rear lights are encouraged.

Questions? Contact Gail Morell.

title: Divorced Dad Support - Peer Support Circle
location: 3820 E Moores Pike, Bloomington, IN 47401
description:
Divorced Dad Support offers Peer Support Circles, where you can connect with other divorced Dads in a safe and confidential space to share experiences, gain insights, and find strength in a community of understanding.

We are committed to:

Open Dialogue: Share experiences and ask questions to gain valuable perspectives from fellow Dads who have walked a similar path.

Guidance: When requested, receive guidance on parenting strategies and self-care during this challenging time.

Confidentiality: Safety is built when we can trust that what we share will remain with the people with whom we choose to share.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. Or a whole day. This self-guided offering is designed to allow you to create your own educational experience. Visit all locations in one trip or come back to campus multiple times. Each Fine Arts Plaza destination has different operating hours; please consult them carefully when planning your trip. All locations are open Tuesday–Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.  Check our online event calendar at go.iu.edu/america-250 (https://go.iu.edu/america-250) for special events and additional campus celebrations of America's 250th.  To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

title: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market
location: City of Bloomington, 401 N Morton St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
The Bloomington Community Farmers' Market takes place rain or shine every Saturday, April through October, at Showers Common next to City Hall, 401 N. Morton St. in Bloomington.
April-September: 8 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
October: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
November: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m. at the Pavilion at Switchyard Park
The Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.
Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. Food and beverage artisans provide a tasteful variety of drinks, pastries, and savory dishes. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.
source: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market, Parks And Rec, WFHB Community Calendar

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

title: Bloomington Community Farmers' Market
location: City of Bloomington, 401 N Morton St, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
The Bloomington Community Farmers' Market takes place rain or shine every Saturday, April through October, at Showers Common next to City Hall, 401 N. Morton St. in Bloomington.
April-September: 8 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
October: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.
November: 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m. at the Pavilion at Switchyard Park
The Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.
Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. Food and beverage artisans provide a tasteful variety of drinks, pastries, and savory dishes. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Common Threads
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Event
description: Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads!  Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time.  This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

description:

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
location: LILLY LIBRARY
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).
source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us.
